title: Effective nonlinear electromagnetism and semiclassical consistency

items.title: A smooth nonlinear electromagnetic constitutive model
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, independent orientation $o$, and the torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ selected by $g$. Fix a smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle sector and a smooth connection $\mathcal A$ in that sector. In the inherited physical-curvature normalization, its curvature is a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $dF=0$. A permitted variation is $\mathcal A_\epsilon=\mathcal A+\epsilon a$, where $a\in\Omega^1(M)$ is smooth and compactly supported; the same-sector convention gives $F_\epsilon=F+\epsilon da$. No global potential is required.

Raise indices with $g^{-1}$ and let $\star_g$ be the Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$. Define the scalar invariants
$$X:=-\frac14 F_{ab}F^{ab},\qquad Y:=-\frac14F_{ab}(\star_gF)^{ab}.$$
Let $L:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$, and write $L_X,L_Y$ for its first partial derivatives evaluated at $(X,Y)$. Define the contravariant antisymmetric tensor
$$H^{ab}:=L_XF^{ab}+L_Y(\star_gF)^{ab}.$$
The source-free local action density is $L(X,Y)\,\mathrm{vol}_g$. Its relative action difference under a compact variation is the integral of $[L(X(F_\epsilon),Y(F_\epsilon))-L(X(F),Y(F))]\,\mathrm{vol}_g$; this difference has compact support even when the unvaried integral over $M$ is not finite. The connection is stationary when the derivative of this relative action at $\epsilon=0$ vanishes for every permitted $a$.

In the mathematical normalization, $L=X$ is the Maxwell quadratic term. If units are attached, the components of $F$ have a fixed unit $\mathfrak F$, $X,Y,L$ have unit $\mathfrak F^2$, and coefficients $\alpha,\beta$ in $L=X+\alpha X^2+\beta Y^2$ have unit $\mathfrak F^{-2}$, so $\alpha X$ and $\beta Y$ are dimensionless. This normalization is not an SI action prefactor. The coefficients are arbitrary parameters, not QED coefficients. This definition supplies no quantum origin, source coupling, characteristic-cone condition, hyperbolicity, causality, or solution-existence claim.

items.title: Constitutive field equation from compact variations
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use the fixed-metric, fixed-bundle-sector data and relative action of the Definition of a smooth nonlinear electromagnetic constitutive model. If the connection is stationary under every smooth compactly supported same-sector variation and the source coupling is absent, then
$$\nabla_aH^{ab}=0,\qquad dF=0.$$
For $L=X+\alpha X^2+\beta Y^2$ this gives
$$H^{ab}=(1+2\alpha X)F^{ab}+2\beta Y(\star_gF)^{ab}.$$
Here $\alpha,\beta$ are arbitrary fixed real parameters with units inverse to those of $X,Y$ when units are attached. This is a conditional Euler–Lagrange deduction for the stated mathematical model; it does not assign QED coefficients or assert that a field solves the equations. The variation alone gives no hyperbolicity, causal-cone, uniqueness, or well-posedness result.

items.title: Conditional semiclassical Einstein–Maxwell source contract
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Fix a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, the metric-selected connection $\nabla$, a smooth real two-form $F$, and constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$ in the inherited SI bookkeeping convention. A unital complex $*$-algebra $\mathfrak A_{g,F}$ means an associative complex algebra with unit $1$ and an antilinear involution satisfying $(AB)^*=B^*A^*$ and $1^*=1$. A state on this algebra means a complex-linear functional $\omega$ such that $\omega(1)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathfrak A_{g,F}$. Choose a specified state class $\mathscr S_{g,F}$ of such states, with any additional regularity conditions stated as part of that choice.

A renormalization prescription $\mathcal R$ is a fixed item of input recording the subtraction rule, scale, and finite local counterterms used for the source assignments. A candidate assignment consists of maps
$$\omega\longmapsto T_{\mathcal R}[g,F,\omega]\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*M),\qquad \omega\longmapsto j_{\mathcal R}[g,F,\omega]\in\Gamma(TM),$$
for $\omega\in\mathscr S_{g,F}$, with smooth spacetime fields. In the inherited SI bookkeeping, $F$ has units $\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $j_{\mathcal R}$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $T_{\mathcal R}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$; these are formal units, not observations. The maps may depend nonlocally on the state.

The assignment is **contract-admissible** when, for every $\omega\in\mathscr S_{g,F}$,
$$\nabla_a j_{\mathcal R}^{a}=0,\qquad \nabla^a T_{\mathcal R,ab}=F_{bc}j_{\mathcal R}^{c}.$$
The current convention is the one in which the classical sourced Maxwell equation is $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ and the Maxwell stress divergence is $\nabla^aT^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}=-F_{bc}j^c$. The identities displayed in this definition are interface conditions; they do not construct $\mathfrak A_{g,F}$, $\mathscr S_{g,F}$, $\mathcal R$, or either source map, and they do not assert that any assignment is contract-admissible.

items.title: Necessary Ward consistency of coupled sources
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, $j\in\Gamma(TM)$, and $T_{\mathrm{ren}}\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*M)$ be smooth, with $\mu_0>0$, $\kappa\ne0$, and constant $\Lambda$. Define
$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\frac12R g_{ab}.$$
Assume the mathematical field equations
$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T_{\mathrm{ren},ab}\right).$$
Then
$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla^aT_{\mathrm{ren},ab}=F_{bc}j^c.$$
These are necessary conditional consequences of the displayed equations and match the contract-admissibility identities of the source-contract Definition; in this item, “Ward consistency” means exactly these two divergence identities. In SI length-coordinate bookkeeping, $[F]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $[j]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_{\mathrm{ren}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and $[\kappa]=\mathrm{s^2\,kg^{-1}m^{-1}}$; the units are formal and no measured value is used. The result asserts no quantum-state construction, renormalized-source existence, or well-posed semiclassical evolution.

items.title: Small invariants do not alone control derivative corrections
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: On oriented Minkowski $\mathbb R^4$ with metric $\eta$, define $X=-F_{ab}F^{ab}/4$ and $Y=-F_{ab}(\star_\eta F)^{ab}/4$ for a smooth real two-form $F$. For fixed finite $\alpha,\beta$, every one-parameter family of smooth exact two-forms with $\sup_{\mathbb R^4}(|\alpha X|+|\beta Y|)\to0$ has uniformly bounded $\sup_{\mathbb R^4}|\partial_xF_{tx}|$. Thus small invariant corrections alone control all derivative scales.
